title: An inseparable element produces a nilpotent after algebraic-closure base change
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $K/k$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $\bar{k}$ be an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\alpha\in K$. If the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$ is inseparable, then $K\otimes_k\bar{k}$ contains a nonzero nilpotent element and is therefore not reduced.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030V (algebra-lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension), together with Tag 030W

proof.text: Let $P\in k[T]$ be the monic minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$. Since $P$ is inseparable, over the algebraic closure $\bar{k}$ it has a repeated root $\beta\in\bar{k}$; write $P=(T-\beta)^2Q$ in $\bar{k}[T]$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030V, field-theory calculation for an inseparable minimal polynomial

proof.text: Put $g=P/(T-\beta)=(T-\beta)Q\in\bar{k}[T]$. The evaluation map $k[T]\to K$, $T\mapsto\alpha$, induces $k[T]/(P)\cong k(\alpha)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso]. After tensoring this isomorphism with $\bar{k}$ over $k$, we identify $k(\alpha)\otimes_k\bar{k}$ with $\bar{k}[T]/(P)$. The class $\bar g$ is nonzero, because $\deg g<\deg P$ so $P$ does not divide $g$, while $\bar g^{\,2}=0$ because $g^2=P Q$ is divisible by $P$. Thus $k(\alpha)\otimes_k\bar{k}$ contains a nonzero nilpotent.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030V, tensor calculation after factoring the inseparable minimal polynomial

proof.text: The inclusion $k(\alpha)\hookrightarrow K$ is injective, and tensoring an injection of $k$-vector spaces with the $k$-vector space $\bar{k}$ remains injective. Hence the induced map $k(\alpha)\otimes_k\bar{k}\to K\otimes_k\bar{k}$ is injective, so the nonzero nilpotent from Step 2 remains nonzero in $K\otimes_k\bar{k}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030V, passage from $k(\alpha)\otimes_k\bar{k}$ to $K\otimes_k\bar{k}$

proof.text: Therefore $K\otimes_k\bar{k}$ has a nonzero nilpotent element. By the definition of a reduced ring, it is not reduced.
